mainTopic: Residue from knives and forbidden fats: knives of עבודה זרה and גוים, cleaning a טריפה knife, and keeping meat apart from חלבים
overview: This amud finishes רב נחמן's case of slaughtering with a knife of עבודה זרה. The גמרא explains that the knife is forbidden but has no residue on it. That works if the knife was only used to cut a branch for the idol, or if it is an old knife heated white-hot. Next, רב says that after slaughtering with a knife of גוים you must peel the meat, and רבה בר בר חנה says rinsing is enough. The גמרא gives two versions of why they argue: the slaughter spot is hot but the סימנים are busy pushing out blood, or the spot is cold but the knife's pressure pushes residue in. רב אחא and רבינא then argue about cleaning a knife used on a טריפה, and the הלכה is that cold water, or even wiping it with a cloth, is enough. רב rules that a butcher needs separate knives and separate rinsing water for meat and חלבים, because of a גזירה, and the requirement itself keeps them from getting mixed up. Finally, אמימר warns not to lay fatty flanks on top of other meat. A new challenge to that rule begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן is talking about a new knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the problem of forbidden residue on the knife by saying רב נחמן means a new knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a new knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from just before: the knife used for slaughter might have forbidden residue on it. It says רב נחמן is talking about a new knife, which has nothing on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the knife carries forbidden fat or residue into the meat. A brand-new knife has never been used, so there is nothing on it to transfer. This answer will be challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: New (a knife that was never used)

phrases.english: With a new [knife].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the residue question from the previous section
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The knife might have forbidden residue that gets into the meat
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a new knife with no residue

steps.title: A new knife should not be forbidden at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a new knife is only an accessory of עבודה זרה, and accessories are not forbidden until they are actually used for worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: A new knife, according to both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, is only an accessory of idol worship. Accessories of idol worship are not forbidden until they are used for worship!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 1. If the knife is new, why would it be a forbidden knife of עבודה זרה in the first place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about when an idol itself becomes forbidden. But for the items that serve an idol, both agree they become forbidden only once they are used for worship. A new, unused knife is therefore not forbidden at all, so there is no case left to talk about.

keyTerms.meaning: Accessories that serve idol worship (not the idol itself)
Until they are used in worship

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא really do argue, but their argument is about the idol itself. About accessories they agree, which is why the גמרא says 'both'.

phrases.english: A new [knife], whether according to Rabbi Yishmael
or according to Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: They argue about when an idol itself becomes forbidden: once it is made, or once it is worshipped.

phrases.english: they are accessories of idol worship,
and accessories of idol worship are not forbidden
until they are used for worship!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָשָׁה, בֵּין לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֵּין לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב נחמן is talking about a new knife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unused accessory is never forbidden, so a new knife cannot be a forbidden knife of עבודה זרה

steps.title: First answer: the knife was used to cut a branch for the idol
steps.stepSummary: The knife was used once for the idol, to cut a branch, which makes it forbidden but leaves no residue.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that he cut a branch for idol worship with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the challenge. The knife was used for the idol only to cut a branch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a branch for the idol counts as using the knife in its service, so it is now a forbidden accessory. But a branch leaves no fat or residue, so the knife is still 'like new' and clean. This solves both problems together.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces a possible answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say,
that he cut a branch with it for idol worship,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דִּפְסַק בֵּיהּ גְּוָוזָא לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A new knife was never used, so it is not forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: It was used only to cut a branch: forbidden, but with no residue

steps.title: Second answer: an old knife heated white-hot in fire
steps.stepSummary: Or, the knife is an old idol knife that was heated until white-hot, which burned off all residue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is an old knife that was heated in fire until it turned white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. The knife really was used for the idol, but the fire cleaned off all residue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old knife used for the idol is truly forbidden as an accessory. Heating it white-hot burns away anything stuck to it. So again the knife is forbidden but carries nothing into the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Heated it in fire until it turned white

steps.whatToRemember: In both answers the knife is forbidden for benefit but has no residue, so רב נחמן's case works.

phrases.english: And if you want, say,
with an old [knife] that he made white-hot in the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same challenge of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A knife without residue must be new and unused
steps.terutzMaskana: An old used knife can also be free of residue after white-hot heating

steps.title: Peel or rinse after slaughtering with a knife of גוים
steps.stepSummary: A new argument: after slaughtering with a knife of גוים, רב says peel the spot, and רבה בר בר חנה says rinse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who slaughters with a knife of גוים. רב said: he peels. רבה בר בר חנה said: he rinses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between two אמוראים. The question is what to do with the meat after slaughtering with a non-Jew's knife, which may have forbidden food stuck to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is stricter: cut a thin layer of meat off the place the knife touched. רבה בר בר חנה is more lenient: just wash that spot. The next step asks what their argument is really based on.

keyTerms.meaning: A knife belonging to non-Jews (likely used for forbidden food)

phrases.english: It was stated: one who slaughters with a knife of gentiles,
Rav said: he peels,
phrases.notes: He peels a thin layer of meat off the place where the knife touched.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: מֵדִיחַ.
phrases.english: and Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: he rinses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about a knife of גוים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: peel the meat. רבה בר בר חנה: rinsing is enough.

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue about whether the slaughter spot is hot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument depends on whether the place of slaughter counts as hot (absorbs) or cold (does not absorb).
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is what they argue about? One holds the place of slaughter is cold, and the other holds it is hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason behind the argument in step 5. This is a proposal that the גמרא is about to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slaughter spot is 'cold', nothing soaks into the meat, so rinsing off the surface is enough (רבה בר בר חנה). If it is 'hot', the residue soaks in, so a layer must be peeled (רב). Heat is what makes food absorb.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is what they argue about?
The place of slaughter on the neck

phrases.english: Shall we say that they argue about this,
that one master holds: the place of slaughter is cold,
phrases.notes: This would be רבה בר בר חנה, who only needs rinsing.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: the place of slaughter is hot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the reason behind the argument in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis of the argument between רב and רבה בר בר חנה?

steps.title: No: everyone agrees the spot is hot, but the סימנים are busy pushing out blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both agree the spot is hot. רבה בר בר חנה holds that the סימנים, busy pushing out blood, do not absorb.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, everyone agrees the place of slaughter is hot. The one who says peel, that is fine. The one who says rinse holds that since the סימנים are busy pushing out blood, they do not absorb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 6. It shows how even רבה בר בר חנה can agree that the spot is hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heat would normally make the meat absorb. But at the moment of slaughter, the windpipe and food pipe are pushing blood outward, and that outward flow stops anything from soaking in. So rinsing the surface is enough, even though the spot is hot.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe and food pipe cut in שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רב and רבה בר בר חנה need not be about hot versus cold. In this first version, the rinse view works because the סימנים are busy pushing out blood and do not absorb. The next step gives a second version.

phrases.english: No, everyone [agrees]
the place of slaughter is hot;
the one who says he peels, that is fine,
and the one who says he rinses,
since the simanim are busy
pushing out blood, they do not absorb.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה רוֹתֵחַ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument is about hot versus cold
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rinse view can hold the spot is hot, because blood flowing outward prevents absorption

steps.title: Second version: the spot is cold, but knife pressure pushes residue in
steps.stepSummary: A second version says everyone agrees the slaughter spot is cold. רבה בר בר חנה's rinsing fits easily. רב requires peeling because the pressure of the knife pushes residue into the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that everyone agrees the slaughter spot is cold. For the one who says to rinse, that makes good sense. The one who says to peel holds that the pressure of the knife makes the meat absorb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way of explaining the argument between רב (peel) and רבה בר בר חנה (rinse). In this version, both agree the slaughter spot is cold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, both sides agreed the spot is hot. Here they both agree it is cold. Cold meat normally does not absorb, so rinsing is enough. רב still requires peeling because the knife presses hard into the flesh, and that pressure alone can push residue in.

keyTerms.meaning: The place on the neck where the animal is slaughtered
Cold, which normally means it does not absorb taste

phrases.english: There are those who say:
phrases.notes: This is a second version of how the argument from steps 5–7 was explained.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees the place of slaughter is cold.
The one who says 'rinse': that works well.
The one who says 'peel':
because of the pressure of the knife, it absorbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה צוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of step 7's rejection: both sides agree the spot is cold instead of hot.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reasoning: the argument is not about hot versus cold but about whether knife pressure causes absorption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument depends on whether the slaughter spot is hot or cold
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree it is cold. רב holds that knife pressure alone causes absorption, so he requires peeling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the step 6 idea that the argument is about hot versus cold
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even if everyone agrees the spot is cold, the peel view holds that the pressure of the knife alone pushes residue into the meat

steps.title: Argument over cleaning a knife used on a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about a knife used to slaughter a טריפה. One says it must be cleaned in hot water, and the other says cold water is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a knife used for a טריפה, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says: in hot water. The other says: in cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument about how to clean a knife that was used to slaughter a טריפה animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden residue is on the knife this time, not on the meat. One opinion holds the knife absorbed forbidden taste and needs hot water to purge it. The other holds that only surface residue is there, so a cold rinse is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A knife used to slaughter a טריפה, an animal with a fatal defect that is forbidden to eat
Hot water, which purges what was absorbed

phrases.english: A knife used for a טריפה:
רב אחא and רבינא disagree about it.
One says: it is cleaned in hot water.
And one says: in cold water.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַכִּין טְרֵיפָה, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from cleaning the meat to cleaning the knife itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dispute over whether a טריפה knife needs hot water or only cold water

steps.title: The הלכה: cold water is enough, and wiping works too
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that cold water is enough. If a torn piece of cloth is available to wipe the knife, even rinsing is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: even in cold water. And if there is a worn piece of curtain to wipe it with, rinsing is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules on the argument: a טריפה knife only needs cold water, and wiping it with a rag is also enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the concern is only surface residue on the knife, not absorbed taste. Anything that removes the surface residue works, whether rinsing or wiping.

keyTerms.meaning: A worn, torn piece of a curtain or cloth

steps.whatToRemember: A knife used on a טריפה only needs its surface residue removed: a cold rinse, or simply wiping it with a cloth.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: even in cold water.
And if there is a worn piece of a curtain
to wipe it with, it is not needed.
phrases.notes: He means rinsing is not needed at all, because wiping is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument from step 9 in favor of cold water.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cold water is enough for a טריפה knife, and wiping it with a cloth also works

steps.title: Challenge: every kosher knife should also need hot water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'hot water' opinion: if the reason is absorbed forbidden residue, then even a knife used on a kosher animal absorbed residue from a living animal (אבר מן החי) during the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says hot water, what is the reason? Because it absorbed something forbidden? A knife used on a permitted animal also absorbed אבר מן החי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the reasoning behind the 'hot water' opinion by showing it would apply to every slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the knife is cutting, the animal is still alive. Its flesh then counts as אבר מן החי, which is forbidden. So if absorbing forbidden residue were the problem, every slaughtering knife would need hot water, not only a טריפה knife.

keyTerms.meaning: Something permitted, here a kosher animal
Flesh or a limb taken from a living animal, which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The animal is not 'kosher' until the שחיטה is finished. During the cutting it is still alive, so its flesh is technically אבר מן החי.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says hot water, what is the reason?
Because it absorbed something forbidden?
A knife used on a permitted animal also absorbed
from a limb of a living animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the 'hot water' opinion from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that a טריפה knife needs hot water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If absorbing forbidden residue requires hot water, every kosher slaughtering knife should need it too, because during the cutting it absorbs אבר מן החי

steps.title: Answer: absorption happens only after the animal is already permitted
steps.stepSummary: The knife only absorbs once the throat heats up, and that happens only when the שחיטה is finished. By then the animal is permitted, so nothing forbidden is absorbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it absorb? When it gets warm. When does it get warm? When the slaughter is finished. At that moment, it is already permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out when the absorbing actually happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Absorption needs heat, and the throat only heats up at the end of the שחיטה. At that moment the animal is no longer אבר מן החי but permitted meat. A טריפה stays forbidden even after the שחיטה, so the question does not apply to it.

phrases.english: When does it absorb? When it gets warm.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַת קָא חָיְימָא? לְכִי גָמְרָה שְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: When does it get warm? When the slaughter is finished.
At that moment, it is already permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing distinction: absorption happens only once the animal is already permitted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A kosher knife absorbs אבר מן החי during the slaughter
steps.terutzMaskana: Heat, and so absorption, comes only at the end of the שחיטה, when the animal is permitted

steps.title: A butcher needs three separate knives
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a butcher needs three knives: one for slaughtering, one for cutting meat, and one for cutting forbidden fats (חלבים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A butcher needs three knives: one to slaughter with, one to cut meat with, and one to cut forbidden fats with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new practical rule about keeping a butcher's knives separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each knife has its own job so that residue does not move from one thing to another. Most importantly, the knife that cuts forbidden fats must not then be used on kosher meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical guideline for butchers: separate tools prevent forbidden residue from reaching kosher meat.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
The butcher needs three knives:
one that he slaughters with,
and one that he cuts meat with,
and one that he cuts forbidden fats with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הַטַּבָּח צָרִיךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה סַכִּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule about knives, continuing the theme of residue on knives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher must keep separate knives for slaughtering, cutting meat, and cutting forbidden fats

steps.title: Why not use one knife, meat first and then fats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב's rule from step 13: why not use one knife for both meat and חלבים, cutting the meat first?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him set aside one knife, cut meat with it, and then cut forbidden fats with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's need for separate knives for meat and חלבים. It suggests a simpler way: one knife, used on the meat first and the fats afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meat is cut first, the knife is still clean when it touches the meat. Fat residue only gets on it afterward. So a second knife seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: let him set aside or prepare

phrases.english: And let him set aside one [knife],
and cut meat with it,
and afterward cut forbidden fats with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for three knives that רב stated in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule requiring a separate knife for חלבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting in the right order with one knife avoids the problem, so a second knife seems unneeded.

steps.title: A decree in case he cuts in the wrong order
steps.stepSummary: חכמים made a גזירה, out of concern that he will cut the fats first and the meat afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he cuts fats and then meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why one knife is not allowed. חז"ל worried that the butcher would sometimes cut the fats first and then the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using one knife in the correct order is fine in principle. But חכמים banned it, because if he forgets the order, fat residue would get onto the meat.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he cut forbidden fats
and afterward meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One knife used in the right order should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים required two knives so that he does not mix up the order.

steps.title: He could mix up the two knives too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even with two knives, he could confuse which knife is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, they will get mixed up for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If he might confuse the order, he might also confuse the two knives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה was meant to prevent a mix-up. But a new mix-up is possible: grabbing the fat knife to cut meat. So the decree seems to solve nothing.

phrases.english: Now too, they will be switched for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the גזירה in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two knives can also be confused, so the decree does not remove the risk of a mix-up.

steps.title: Requiring two knives makes him alert
steps.stepSummary: Because חכמים required two knives, he has a clear sign that keeps them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they required him to have two, he has a clear marker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule itself prevents confusion. Once he must keep two separate knives, he pays attention to which is which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one knife, the only safeguard is remembering the order, which is easy to forget. With two required knives there is a clear distinction, such as a mark on one, so mixing them up is unlikely.

phrases.english: Since they required him [to have] two,
he has a recognizable sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two knives can be confused just as easily as the order of cutting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two required knives give him a clear sign, so confusion is unlikely.
steps.whatToRemember: A butcher needs a separate knife for חלבים. This is a גזירה, and the requirement itself creates a היכרא that prevents mix-ups.

steps.title: Two water vessels: one for meat, one for fats
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a butcher needs two vessels of water, one to rinse meat and one to rinse חלבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in רב's name: the butcher needs two vessels of water, one to rinse meat in and one to rinse fats in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second rule from רב, similar to the knives. Rinsing water also has to be kept separate for meat and fats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water used on forbidden fat may carry fat residue. Rinsing meat in it could transfer that residue, so separate vessels are required.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: הַטַּבָּח צָרִיךְ שְׁנֵי כֵּלִים שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: The butcher needs two vessels of water,
one in which he rinses meat,
and one in which he rinses forbidden fats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling of רב, applying the knife idea to rinsing water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher must have separate water vessels for rinsing meat and rinsing חלבים.

steps.title: Why not one vessel, meat first and then fats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one vessel would not work, rinsing meat first and fats afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him set aside one vessel, rinse meat in it, and then rinse fats in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge as with the knives, now about the water. Rinse the meat first while the water is still clean, then the fats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meat is rinsed before any fat touches the water, the meat stays clean, so a second vessel seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: And let him set aside one [vessel],
and rinse meat in it,
and afterward rinse forbidden fats in it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two-vessel rule in step 18, in the same way step 14 challenged the knives.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement of two water vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rinsing in the right order with one vessel avoids the problem.

steps.title: A decree in case he rinses in the wrong order
steps.stepSummary: Again a גזירה: he might rinse fats first and meat afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he rinses fats and then meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as with the knives. חכמים feared he would rinse in the wrong order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One vessel is fine only if he always keeps the order. Since he might forget, חכמים required two vessels.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he rinse forbidden fats
and afterward meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One vessel used in the right order should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two vessels are required so that he does not mix up the order.

steps.title: He could mix up the two vessels too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two vessels could also be confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, they will get mixed up for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The same pushback as with the knives. Two vessels can also get mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about confusion seems to apply equally to two vessels, so the גזירה seems not to help.

phrases.english: Now too, they will be switched for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two vessels can be confused just like the order of rinsing.

steps.title: Requiring two vessels gives him a clear sign
steps.stepSummary: Because two vessels are required, he has a היכרא that keeps them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they required him to have two, he has a clear marker.
steps.whatsHappening: Same answer as before. The required separation keeps him aware of which vessel is which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A formal requirement for two vessels makes the difference obvious, while relying on order alone is easy to forget.

phrases.english: Since they required him [to have] two,
he has a recognizable sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two vessels can be confused easily.
steps.terutzMaskana: Requiring two vessels creates a היכרא that prevents confusion.
steps.whatToRemember: Knives and rinsing water follow the same pattern: separate ones for meat and חלבים because of a גזירה, and the requirement itself prevents mix-ups.

steps.title: Don't lay the flanks on top of other meat
steps.stepSummary: אמימר, quoting רב פפא, rules that flanks should not be placed on top of other meat, because their fat drips and the meat absorbs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in רב פפא's name: a person should not place the flanks on top of meat, because the fat drips and the meat absorbs it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule about storing meat. The flanks carry forbidden fat, so they should not rest on top of other meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidden fat can melt and drip down. Whatever meat lies underneath would absorb it and become a problem.

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: לָא לִיסְחוֹף אִינִישׁ כַּפְלֵי עִילָּוֵי בִּישְׂרָא,
phrases.english: A person should not place the flanks on top of meat,
because the fat drips and the meat absorbs it.
phrases.notes: The flanks have forbidden fat attached. That fat is what drips down onto the meat below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule, still about keeping חלבים away from permitted meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flanks with forbidden fat should not be placed on top of other meat.

steps.title: Then even flanks in their normal position should be a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if fat drips into meat, then even when the flank lies normally, its fat should drip into the flank's own meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even when they lie in their normal position, the fat should drip and the meat absorb it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's concern. In a flank lying normally, the fat sits on top of the flank's own meat, so the same dripping should happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dripping fat is really a concern, the flank itself should be a problem, since its fat sits right above its own meat. Yet no one forbids the flank meat.

keyTerms.meaning: placed in the normal, upright way

phrases.english: If so, when they lie in their normal way too,
the fat drips and the meat absorbs it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's reasoning that fat drips into meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same dripping should happen inside the flank itself in its normal position.

steps.title: A membrane separates the fat from below
steps.stepSummary: A membrane lies under the fat and blocks it from reaching the flank's own meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The membrane separates it from below!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that inside the flank there is a membrane between the fat and the meat. It stops the fat from dripping into the meat beneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the normal position, the membrane is under the fat and protects the meat. If the flank is laid on other meat, the fat touches that meat directly with nothing in between.

phrases.english: The membrane separates from below!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The flank's own meat should absorb its fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A membrane under the fat protects the flank's meat, but not other meat placed underneath.

steps.title: A new challenge begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another challenge with 'if so', which continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new challenge to the membrane answer, and the rest of it comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אי הכי' signals that the גמרא will draw a problem from the membrane answer. We have to wait for the next lines to see what the problem is.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: The rest of this question continues in the next section of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the membrane answer in step 25.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated; it continues in the next section.
